questions.prompt: One-way ANOVA: k = 3 groups, n = 4 observations per group. The df pair (df₁, df₂) is:
questions.explain: df₁ = k−1 = **2** (numerator, between groups); df₂ = k(n−1) = 3×(4−1) = **9** (denominator, within groups). Drill P1's variants: k=3, n=5 → (2, 12) with F(0.05) = 3.885; k=4, n=6 → (3, 20) with F(0.05) = 3.098. Get the df pair right FIRST — the whole lookup depends on it.

options: If any mean differs, the BETWEEN-group variance inflates, pushing F upward — only large F is evidence against H₀
questions.explain: F = between-variance / within-variance. Mean deviations in ANY direction INCREASE the between-group variance — they can never decrease it. So evidence against H₀ only accumulates in the right tail.

questions.prompt: Group means 12.5, 16.5, 10.5 (n = 4 each), s_x̄² = 9.333. Between-group estimate = n·s_x̄² = ?
questions.explain: n·s_x̄² = 4 × 9.333 = **37.333**. Within = mean of group variances = 1.667. **F₀ = 37.333/1.667 = 22.400** vs F(0.05; 2, 9) = 4.256 → reject: machines differ (ANOVA only says 'not all equal').

questions.prompt: SSD brands: between = 22.733, within = 30.611. Compute F₀ (3 decimals).
questions.explain: F₀ = 22.733/30.611 = **0.743** < F(0.05; 3, 16) = 3.239 → fail to reject. **F < 1 means the groups differ LESS than their internal noise predicts** — automatic fail-to-reject (critical values are always > 1).

questions.prompt: Designs: means 82.6, 71.8, 88.2 (n = 5 each); s_x̄² = 69.493; group variances 15.8, 8.2, 8.2. Compute F₀ (1 decimal).
Select the THREE assumptions of one-way ANOVA:
questions.explain: **Normality + equal variances + independent random samples.** (Equal sample means is what the TEST checks, not an assumption!)

questions.source: Drill CH8 P6(ii) — why not many t-tests
questions.prompt: Why use ANOVA instead of running all pairwise t-tests?
options: Multiple t-tests inflate the family-wise Type I error (6 tests at α=0.05 ≈ 26% false-alarm chance); ANOVA tests all means at once at one α
questions.explain: **Error inflation** is the reason. And the flip side (P6(iii)): a significant ANOVA only says **at least one mean differs** — identifying which needs post-hoc comparisons (not in this syllabus).
